errors.notFoundBody: That address does not match anything in this interface.

problems.emptyBody: Every host and service is in its OK state.
problems.emptyFilteredBody: Nothing matches the current filters. Widen them to see more.
problems.hideSymptomsTitle: Hide services whose host is down. They are usually a consequence of that host, not a separate incident.
problems.hostDownTitle: The host this service runs on is down, so this is probably a symptom.

downtimes.flexibleTitle: A flexible downtime starts when the object first goes down inside the window, not at the scheduled time.
downtimes.emptyHistoryBody: No maintenance window has finished yet, or the worker has aged them out.

acknowledgements.stickyTitle: A sticky acknowledgement survives the state getting worse.
acknowledgements.emptyBody: Nobody has taken ownership of a problem yet.

logentries.emptyBody: Nothing in this window. If this stays empty, check that LogData is enabled in statusengine.toml — the broker does not publish log lines by default.

range.label: Range
range.tooWide: Wider than this view allows. Name a host to raise the limit.

dashboard.unhandledOf: {{unhandled}} of {{problems}} problems are waiting for someone
dashboard.allClearBody: Every problem is either acknowledged or inside a maintenance window.
dashboard.stale: No update for {{since}} — the worker or the monitoring core may have stopped

detail.noServicesBody: This host has no service checks.
detail.hostNotFoundBody: The monitoring core does not know a host called {{host}}.
detail.serviceNotFoundBody: There is no service called {{service}} on {{host}}.

metrics.title: Performance data
metrics.noneAtAll: This service's plugin does not emit performance data, so there is nothing to chart.
metrics.emptyWindowBody: This service has data going back {{since}}. Widen the range to reach it.

history.scopedHint: Scoped to one object, so the range may go back up to 90 days.
history.unscopedHint: Across every object the range is capped at 6 hours. Name a host to widen it to 90 days — the history tables are stored per object, so a scoped query is far cheaper.
history.repeatTitle: A retry that found the same state again, not a transition.
history.timedOutTitle: The plugin hit its timeout and was killed.
history.emptyChecksBody: Nothing ran in the selected range, or the worker has aged these records out.
history.emptyStatesTitle: No state changes in this window
history.emptyStatesBody: Nothing changed state in the selected range. This table stays empty unless StateChange is enabled in statusengine.toml.
history.emptyNotificationsBody: Nobody was notified in the selected range.

live.liveTitle: Changes arrive from the monitoring core as they happen.
live.pollingTitle: The live stream is not available, so this page refreshes every 30 seconds. Everything still works.
live.offlineTitle: Neither the live stream nor polling is getting through. Check the connection to the server.

commands.disabled: External commands are switched off on this deployment: the worker has no command API key.
commands.nothingToAcknowledge: There is nothing to acknowledge while this is in its OK state.
commands.acknowledgeExplainer: Stops notifications for this problem and records who took it. It clears by itself when the object recovers.
commands.downtimeExplainer: Suppresses notifications for the window. The object keeps being checked and keeps showing its real state.
commands.resultExplainer: Hands the monitoring core a check result as if a plugin had produced it. The core applies its normal retry and notification logic.
commands.notifyExplainer: Sends a message to this object's contacts, outside the normal notification rules.
commands.downtimeCommentPlaceholder: What is happening during this window?
commands.noSemicolons: No semicolons: Naemon splits command fields on them.
commands.stickyHelp: Keep the acknowledgement if the state gets worse.
commands.notifyContactsHelp: Send a notification that this was acknowledged.
commands.persistentHelp: Leave the comment in place after the object recovers.
commands.allServices: Include every service on this host
commands.allServicesHelp: A host downtime does not cover its services on its own.
commands.notifyPlaceholder: What do the contacts need to know?
commands.forcedHelp: Ignore disabled notifications and active downtimes.
commands.broadcastHelp: Send to every contact, not only those who would normally be notified.
commands.confirming: Submitted. Waiting for the monitoring core.
commands.submittedNote: The command reached the message broker.
commands.notConfirmedNote: The command reached the message broker, but {{target}} has not changed yet. The core may still be working through its queue.

bulk.selectPage: Select every row on this page

context.overlapping: {{count}} windows overlap here. Notifications stay suppressed until the last of them ends.
context.notStickyTitle: The acknowledgement clears by itself if the state gets worse.
context.ackWithoutRecord: The monitoring core reports this as acknowledged, but no record of who set it reached the database.

audit.emptyBody: As soon as somebody submits a command it appears here, with who sent it, what it was aimed at and how it went.
audit.emptyFilteredBody: Different filters or a wider window will probably turn something up.
